review.summary: This PR adds POST request tests for the things_advanced example and updates the example to use bounded_stream. The core test additions look reasonable, but there are correctness concerns: the README diff mistakenly changes the signature of StorageError.handle to (req, resp, ex, params), which is wrong for Falcon's exception handler signature in older versions. The FAQ example also has a subtle bug where reading from req.stream may consume nothing when Content-Length is fabricated, and the example app change from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() is a behavioral change that warrants explanation in the news fragment. The tests themselves are reasonable but minimal.

issues.description: README changes StorageError.handle signature, possibly breaking handler contract
issues.detail: The README diff changes handle(ex, req, resp, params) to handle(req, resp, ex, params). Falcon's add_error_handler historically expects (ex, req, resp, params) for older versions and may not match the new signature on all supported versions. This change in documentation could mislead users; verify it matches the framework's current handler contract.

issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is a behavior change without changelog
issues.detail: examples/things_advanced.py changes body = req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read(). This is a meaningful behavioral change (bounded vs raw stream) for users following the example. No towncrier news fragment is included for the example change, despite the PR checklist claiming one was added. Document the rationale.

issues.description: FAQ example PostTest reads from req.stream instead of bounded_stream
issues.detail: The FAQ example uses req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) which contradicts the example fix in things_advanced.py that switched to bounded_stream for safety. For consistency and to avoid hangs on missing/wrong Content-Length, the FAQ example should also use bounded_stream, especially given it's meant as guidance.

issues.description: FAQ code example has style issues: missing blank line, unnecessary parens in assert
issues.detail: The FAQ Python snippet uses `assert(result.status == ...)` with parentheses (treats assert as a function call, a common Python anti-pattern). Also the trailing comma in `headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),]` and missing blank line between class and decorator are stylistically inconsistent with the rest of the codebase shown in README cleanup.

issues.description: Test resp3 relies on hardcoded UUID-generated location not being asserted
issues.detail: The new test asserts only resp3.status_code == 201 but doesn't verify the Location header or that the thing was actually stored. Given this test exists to demonstrate successful POST behavior, asserting on resp3.headers.get('Location') containing '/1337/things/' would catch routing regressions.

issues.description: README scope creep: unrelated style/formatting reflow mixed with test PR
issues.detail: The PR is titled 'add POST request tests' but includes extensive README.rst reformatting (line wrapping, removed blank lines, code_to_http_status change, percent-format to .format conversion). These cosmetic changes are unrelated to the stated goal and make review harder. Consider splitting into separate commits/PRs.
